findings.title: No contract renders the agents, and the skill loses its `nio agents sync`
quotes: plan the gate, render the agents and write each planned lens's pack to `.nio/runs/<run>/jury/packs/<lens>.md`
Start a run with `nio run`, and run `nio agents sync` so every `nio-<lens>` agent exists.
steps 2–5 and 8 become one loop: plan and add your own triggers (`nio jury plan`, `nio pack`, `--add`), then run `nio jury next <slug> <gate> [--add ...]`
findings.fix: in CT-1 case 2, call `agents.sync(root)` before writing packs (and refuse on its errors), or keep `nio agents sync` as a named step in CT-6's loop. Add a TC asserting that the rendered juror files grant Write after a step.

sources.situation: today step 2 of the skill runs `agents.sync` before any juror starts. CT-1's shape only "calls `collect` and `check` in turn", and CT-2 only writes packs and step.json. Neither calls `agents.sync`, and CT-6 folds step 2 into the loop without keeping the sync. CT-5 changes every juror card to `tools: [read, write]`, so a project whose `.claude/agents/nio-*.md` were rendered before this change keeps read-only jurors. Those jurors can't write the output file the pack asks for, so the orchestrator has to save each answer again or the gate stalls on `no output`.

findings.reason: FR-12 (spec.md:104) says the step renders the agents, but CT-1 (it calls only `collect` and `check`), CT-2 (writes packs and step.json) and CT-6 (folds step 2 into the loop) never call `agents.sync`. Cards already rendered read-only stay read-only after CT-5 changes the juror cards.
findings.note: CT-1 case 2 calls agents.sync first (FR-12 already says so); TC-12 asserts the rendered nio-logic grants Write

findings.title: The escalation `next:` always uses a `fixcheck --blocker` pack, and its output file is named in no pack
quotes: next: escalate <lens>: run 2 more jurors on nio jury fixcheck <slug> <gate> --lens <lens> --blocker J-n, outputs <gate>-<lens>-2.md and <gate>-<lens>-3.md
each with a fresh pack (after the first review, the blocker's pack, `nio jury fixcheck <slug> spec --lens <lens> --blocker J-<n>`)
Write your whole output to the file your pack names, and to no other file; never edit the files you judge.
findings.fix: have CT-1 pick the pack by phase, as the skill does. Have the step (CT-2) write `packs/<lens>-2.md` and `packs/<lens>-3.md`, each ending with the `## Your output` line for its `-2`/`-3` file, or explicitly assign this to the orchestrator in CT-6.

sources.situation: the skill, which CT-6 says keeps escalation, gives first-review escalation jurors a fresh first-review pack and uses the `--blocker` pack only after the first review. CT-1 sends every escalation to the `--blocker` pack. That pack is built from `fixcheck`'s lines, which name no output file, and the step doesn't write it. So under CT-5's card sentence the juror has no file to write. The first-review pack the step does write (`packs/<lens>.md`) names `<gate>-<lens>.md`, so reusing it would overwrite the original juror's output.

findings.reason: CT-1's escalation `next:` always points at `nio jury fixcheck ... --blocker`, but skill step 5 uses that pack only after the first review. CT-2 writes no `-2`/`-3` pack and appends no `## Your output` line to a fixcheck pack, so under CT-5's card sentence the escalation juror has no output file named.
findings.note: CT-1 escalation line: the orchestrator copies the right pack per phase with the -2/-3 output line; escalation stays the skill's

findings.title: CT-2's run rules clash with the refuter pack and with TC-5(a)
quotes: A run whose `packs/step.json` exists is never rewritten. Before starting a new run for a re-review, the step reuses a run whose `step.json` holds the same gate, round and version and which has no output yet.
a refuter batch printed → CT-2 writes its pack; `next: run nio-refuter on .nio/runs/<run>/jury/packs/refuter.md
(a) `gate_spec()`, `first = step(root)`; (b) TC-2's state after its action, `second = step(root, run)`.
(a) both print `run: <run_of(first)>` and the same `next:` line

findings.note: CT-2: lens packs and step.json never rewritten, refuter.md per batch; reuse rule covers any step without --run

findings.title: The escalation trigger counts jurors the ledger keeps across rounds
quotes: a lens with a confirmed open blocker and fewer than 3 jurors of that lens
juror = led["jurors"].setdefault(path.stem, {"attempts": 0})
findings.fix: count only the lens's jurors whose `round` is the current round (or that judged this blocker), and add a TC for a second escalation in a later round.

sources.situation: `merge` keys jurors by file stem and never removes them, so `spec-logic-2` and `spec-logic-3` stay in `led["jurors"]` after the first escalation. In a later re-review where the refuter confirms a new blocker from logic, CT-1 sees 3 jurors of that lens, skips escalation, and composes the outcome. The skill's step 5 escalates every confirmed blocker.

findings.note: CT-1 counts only the lens's jurors of the current round

findings.title: TC-19 expects an outcome line that CT-1 and TC-1 say the step never prints with a batch pending
quotes: the step prints the same `outcome:` line as the hand-run check, writes no second verdict record, and its `next:` line is the refuter action (the batch still pending).
no outcome line (`outcome:`) is printed.
a refuter batch printed → CT-2 writes its pack;
if record and outcome in ("approved", "rejected", "human") and entry not in led["recorded"]:
findings.fix: In TC-19, assert that the step prints no `outcome:` line and that its `next:` is the refuter action. For the no-second-record check, use a state that records, such as TC-2's `rejected` state with the hand-run `check`.

sources.situation: In TC-1's state, J-1 is pending. `collect` prints the refuter batch even when nothing new was collected, so the step takes CT-1's refuter branch and never calls `check`. A step built to CT-1 and TC-1 prints no `outcome:` line, so TC-19 fails. A step that prints one to satisfy TC-19 breaks TC-1. Separately, the hand-run `check` composes `pending`, which is never recorded, so "writes no second verdict record" holds whatever the step does.

findings.reason: `collect` (jury.py:646-652) prints the refuter batch whenever a finding is pending, so CT-1 takes the refuter branch and never calls `check`. The step therefore prints no `outcome:` line, which contradicts TC-19's "same `outcome:` line" and agrees with TC-1's "no outcome line".
findings.note: TC-19 asserts no outcome line while the batch is pending; the no-second-record check moved to TC-2's rejected state

lens = meta.get("lens", path.stem.split("-", 1)[1])
findings.fix: Give the escalation file a front matter that disagrees with its file name, such as `lens_name="logic-2"`. Today that files it under `logic-2`, so the test fails before the work. Then assert the juror's lens is `logic` and that exactly one mismatch line names `spec-logic-2.md`.

sources.situation: The fixture's front matter already says `lens: logic`, and today's `merge` takes the lens from the front matter. So `led["jurors"]["spec-logic-2"]["lens"] == "logic"` passes before any work, and "no mismatch line" passes because today's code prints none. Nothing in the test depends on the file name.

findings.reason: The test helper writes `lens: {lens_name or name}` (test_jury.py:34), so TC-10's front matter says `logic`. Today's `merge` (jury.py:688) already takes the lens from `meta.get("lens")`, so the assertion and "no mismatch line" both pass before the work.
findings.note: TC-10 front matter says logic-2, so it fails on today's code

`calls <= 15` (it is 13)
nor to run `nio jury collect` or `nio jury fixcheck` itself, except for escalation (`--blocker`)

findings.fix: In TC-18, assert that `## Steps` names none of `nio run`, `nio agents sync`, `nio jury template`, `nio jury check`, `nio jury changed` outside the escalation and closure text. Make TC-11's script follow the skill's steps, including `nio jury plan` and the gate check, and state that count.

sources.situation: TC-11 counts a fixed script the test writes itself, so `calls <= 15` can only fail if the test is edited. TC-18 rules out only `collect`, `fixcheck` and the save-answer sentence. A shipped skill that still tells the orchestrator to run `nio run`, `nio agents sync`, `nio jury template`, `nio jury check --record` after each step, and `nio jury changed` before the re-review passes both tests while needing well over 15 calls. The count also leaves out calls the CT-6 loop itself names: "plan and add your own triggers (`nio jury plan`, `nio pack`, `--add`)", and `nio check spec --gate` before the re-review.

findings.reason: TC-11 counts a script the test writes itself, and TC-18 only forbids `collect`, `fixcheck` and the save-answer sentence. A skill that still names `nio run`, `nio agents sync`, `nio jury template`, `nio jury check` or `nio jury changed` passes both tests, and the count leaves out the `nio jury plan` and gate-check calls that CT-6 names.
findings.note: TC-18 lists every command the steps must no longer name; TC-11 follows the skill's steps from nio jury plan (14 calls); CT-6 names the dropped calls

sources.situation: In TC-11 the re-review run holds packs and outputs only for testability and logic. The planned consistency lens has no `spec-consistency.md` in that run, so the new first branch prints `next: re-run consistency` and never calls `check`. `outcome: approved` can't be reached, and any re-review that skips a lens repeats this every time. The same happens in TC-14(b) for the lenses its fix check leaves out.

In TC-11 the re-review run holds packs and outputs only for testability and logic. The planned consistency lens has no `spec-consistency.md` in that run, so the first branch prints `next: re-run consistency` and never calls `check`. `outcome: approved` can't be reached, and any re-review that skips a lens repeats this every time. The same happens in TC-14(b) for the lenses its fix check leaves out.

A re-review run holds packs only for the lenses `changed()` names, which are the lenses with a fixed finding (jury.py line 446). Every other planned lens has no `<gate>-<lens>.md` in that run, so CT-1's first branch prints `next: re-run <lens>` and `step` never reaches the check. In TC-11 that is the third planned lens (consistency, per the situation given in J-10), so the expected `outcome: approved` can't be reached. TC-14(b) hits the same thing for the lenses its fix check leaves out, and every re-review that skips a lens repeats the loop.

findings.reason: The quoted first branch of CT-1 counts every planned lens with no `<gate>-<lens>.md` in this run as missing. A re-review run holds packs and outputs only for the lenses `changed()` names (jury.py:437-457, which returns just those with a fix to check), so any other planned lens, such as consistency in TC-11, would print `next: re-run <lens>`. `step` would then never reach `check`, and TC-11's `outcome: approved` could not be reached. The code's own missing check, `[lens for lens in led["expect"] if lens not in lenses]` at jury.py:964, is scoped to the ledger's `expect`, not to every planned lens, and nothing in the quoted text narrows the branch the same way. The finding is judged against the earlier text, as you asked. I did not re-read the edited contracts.md. This is the same finding as the two escalation re-raises, with no other duplicate.
findings.note: CT-1: only lenses this run has a pack for (step.json lenses) count as missing; TC-11 asserts no re-run consistency after the fix-check packs
